answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is stake-weighted attestation history: each agent must lock tokens that flow like a river into a shared pool, and only those with consistent positive peer scores over many epochs can act as a beacon of trust. A cheap flood of new identities fails because forging a long coherent record requires real capital and time, much as a single forced sonnet cannot replace years of genuine craft. This makes mass identity creation economically prohibitive.
